_comment: SDR fleet policy v2.1 (SB7, 2026-07-05) — SINGLE-HOST on the M1 Mac mini (host confirmed by Will; Intel mini = cold spare). Source of truth for device->role allocation, RSPduo modes, USB grouping, and tuner-broker invariants. The broker, config generators, and wiring card all read THIS file. Address devices by serial ONLY; USB position is never trusted. Digital engine = SDRTrunk (native SDRplay API; it MUST still claim its serial(s) through the broker so nothing else opens the device). op25 is retired (no macOS path). See docs/sb7-northstar-program.md §4.

host.cold_spare: Mac mini 2018 Intel (16 GB, macOS Sequoia ceiling — security updates end ~fall 2027)

digital_capacity._primary: RSP-A in SDRTrunk native Dual Tuner mode = 2 P25 systems at once, one per ~2 MHz tuner. MTRTRS ships first on tuner 1; the 2nd system slots onto tuner 2 (Will to name it). Each system's monitored SITE must fit ~2 MHz — verify spans in SDRangel before committing (a single trunked site's control+traffic normally fits well under 2 MHz; statewide spread does NOT matter because you monitor one site).
digital_capacity.growth_to_3: A 3rd P25 system = add RTL 'DIGITAL-FLEX' (70613472) to the SAME SDRTrunk instance (heterogeneous tuners are supported). The broker leases that RTL to SDRTrunk on demand; drops disco/hot-spare use of it while active.
digital_capacity._0x6bed_safe: RSP-A dual + RSP-B single-tuner through ONE apiService is compliant (max_concurrent_dual_tuner_rspduo=1). The never-tested combo here is SDRTrunk(native API) + chirp(SoapySDRPlay3) sharing one apiService — validate in the SB7.1 soak before trusting 24/7.

invariants._why: Two concurrent dual-tuner RSPduos through ONE sdrplay apiService deterministically segfault it (0x6bed) and corrupt live IQ. Single host = single apiService, so exactly one device (RSP-A) may be dual-tuner; the broker REFUSES any second dual-tuner claim. RSP-B stays single-tuner.
invariants._why_gap: The apiService does not safely serialize concurrent sdrplay_api_Open calls from different processes, even across different physical RSPduos.

rspduo_daemon._note: One apiService brokers BOTH RSPduos: chirp airband via SoapySDRPlay3, SDRTrunk digital via the native API. All opens funnel through the tuner-broker, spaced by rspduo_open_gap_sec. SDRTrunk launches once and stays up (KeepAlive) — no restart churn near this daemon.

devices.label: RSP-DIGITAL

tuners._note: D3 launch target. Pin the MTRTRS control channel to this tuner via SDRTrunk's per-channel Preferred Tuner.
2nd P25 system — Will names it. Slots on here with no hardware change; SDRTrunk restart to add. Verify its site span fits ~2 MHz.

devices._note: SDRTrunk native Dual Tuner — NOT osmosdr mode=MA/SL (that was op25, retired). No device_args; SDRTrunk manages both tuners internally from its playlist. The broker leases the ONE serial 180903EF32 to SDRTrunk (dual_tuner=true consumes the single allowed dual slot).

devices.label: RSP-AIRBAND
devices._note: ST = the proven-clean airband config (2026-06-15). chirp calls set_bandwidth explicitly (chirp/dsp/source_sdr.py) — keep bandwidth_hz set even though ST tolerates a driver default.

devices.serial_status: confirmed-on-micro; re-verify + reflash if needed in SB7.1
devices.label: GROUND
devices._note: FIXED, 24/7 core analog. Ground NFM on RTL is the proven 2026-06-18 fix. Stable dongle chosen deliberately. Gain 30-35 (40 clips the V4-class front end).

devices.label: DIGITAL-FLEX
devices._note: The growth path to a 3rd P25 system. Stable dongle (a digital control channel needs reliability). Default idle role = disco sweep / hot-spare; broker promotes it to SDRTrunk's 3rd system when Will activates one.

devices.label: WX
devices._note: Weather decoders (VDL2 / ACARS). Drop-tolerant. Can be surrendered to hot-spare if a dedicated dongle dies.

devices.serial_status: confirmed-on-micro (RTL-SDR Blog V4, USB-finicky — error -71 re-enumeration history)
devices.label: WATERFALL
devices._note: Live IQ waterfall (/sb5), SINGLE-dongle mode (~2.4 MHz span). The flaky V4 lands here on purpose — the waterfall is drop-tolerant, digital/analog decode is not. Put it on the best hub port. NOTE: this is a step down from the old 2-dongle stitched waterfall — that RTL was reallocated to DIGITAL-FLEX to serve Will's '≥2 digital systems, room for 3' requirement. If Will prefers the wide stitched waterfall over a 3rd digital system, swap RTL-DIGFLEX back to waterfall-B.

G1._note: RSP-A (dual-tuner, heaviest) direct-cabled, own controller, no hub

G2._note: RSP-B direct-cabled, own controller, no hub

G3._note: 4 RTLs on a powered hub. VERIFY on the box with `system_profiler SPUSBDataType`: the M1's two USB-A ports may share one controller — if so, 4 RTLs on one controller is within max_rtl_streams_per_usb_controller=5 but near it; consider splitting across a 2nd powered hub on the other USB-A port if throughput/overflow shows up in the SB7.1 soak.
